memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares, bullish on the business; conviction medium. Bufab (BUFAB-SE) is a self-help margin case that has completed and is now priced as a compounder: at SEK 145.40 (2026-09-23) the shares already pay for the margin, the organic recovery and the announced deals, so the modal return is about 4 percent a year over three years and about 0 percent over eighteen months against the 20 percent bar. The gate does not park the case (no D or F on management B, business quality B, predictability C or trackability C); the return does. What re-opens it: a price below about SEK 110 with the earnings path intact (the three-year value of SEK 163.8 discounted at 20 percent a year is about SEK 95; the eighteen-month value of SEK 145.3 discounted for 1.5 years is about SEK 110; with the multiple held at 25.9x the three-year figure gives about SEK 109), or the three Key Drivers going right over two quarters with a cohort re-rating that lifts Addtech, Lagercrantz and Lifco toward 30x. What to watch: the Q3 report on 2026-10-23 for gross margin above 32.5 percent and organic growth above 4 percent; deal announcements in H2 2026; the price against SEK 110.
case: The thesis. Bufab is a self-help margin case that has completed and is now priced as a compounder. At SEK 145.40 the shares already pay for the margin, the organic recovery and the announced deals, so what is left on the modal path is about 4 percent a year against the 20 percent bar. The business is compelling; the investment at this price is not; the same case at SEK 95 to 110 a share would be.

The change is internal, dated and real. A new chief executive in August 2022 repriced the product on the value it delivers rather than its cost, raised the adjusted EBITA margin target from 12 to 14 percent in December 2023, sold the manufacturing units in 2024 and 2025 and redirected acquisitions to platforms with margins above 14 percent. The screen's decision rule is met twice over (chief-executive change plus guidance increase; at least three further strong forces: standards improvement A, price rises A, strategy B, perimeter B, acquisitions B). No false-positive red flag fits: twelve quarters of gross-margin data say it is not a slide-deck transformation; the units sold were about 5 percent of sales; leverage 2.4x is inside target; no debt-funded buyback. The internal forces are B, not A, because they are mature: the 14 percent target is already exceeded at 15.0 percent for H1 2026 and no new target has been set, so the next raise, if any, is the force the market would be waiting for; the remaining levers (working capital, the acquisition pace) are the ones management calls "not a quick fix".

The external forces are mixed and do not carry the case (C). No force meets the 'Demand Inflection' test: European PMIs are below 50 and the sell-side wants three to four prints above 50 before calling a turn. Tailwinds are niche-level or regulatory (defence and aerospace, semiconductor equipment, nearshoring, CBAM as a barrier for small distributors); headwinds are live (construction, kitchens, automotive, FX, freight). Q2 2026 organic growth of 5.3 percent was, in the chief executive's words, primarily market-share gains and the ramp of previously secured large contracts (Babcock in the UK; a semiconductor-equipment customer), not a broad recovery. Direction by force: demand mixed (C); competition easing through consolidation (B); disruption being disproved for the recurring, traceability-mandatory 90 percent of purchases (B); political and regulatory two-edged, net tailwind for scale (C); supply side neutral to slight headwind (C); the company's own cycle turning up (B: organic minus 5.4 percent 2024, plus 0.3 percent 2025, plus 2.2 percent Q1 2026, plus 5.3 percent Q2 2026); macro a headwind (D: over half of sales on European industrial production; the unhedged USD mismatch). The Swedish compounder cohort is itself a force on the multiple (Lifco fell 16 percent on a short report; the cohort de-rated about 11 percent over the twelve months to July 2026).
counter_case: The bull's case, at full force: Bufab has become a Swedish compounder and deserves the set's multiple of about 28x rather than a discount, and it will compound EPS at the 15 percent a year it targets, as it did at 17 percent a year for the decade to 2025, through acquired growth of 8 percent a year (the sell-side's model), organic growth of 4 to 5 percent, margins to 16 percent and operating leverage. On that path FY2028 EPS is DNB Carnegie's SEK 6.22, the 24-month-forward figure at September 2029 is about SEK 9.15, and at 28x the shares are worth about SEK 256 plus SEK 5.15 of dividends, plus 80 percent, about 21.6 percent a year, clearing the bar; even with the multiple held at 25.9x it is about SEK 237 plus SEK 5.15, about 18.5 percent a year. The evidence for it: the 17 percent record; three consecutive beats; a fragmented market with targets at 6 to 7.5x EV/EBITA; CBAM as a hidden organic driver; the earnings review's own 25 percent-plus internal-rate-of-return conclusion; a sell-side outer-year revenue growth of 5.8 percent (FY2028) and 5.7 percent (FY2029) that is mechanically too low for a serial acquirer because the FactSet median drops deals until announced, which is a named mis-modelled line, a proven upgrader and a B-quality business, the three conditions of 'Compounder' as the primary pattern with its payoff still ahead. On this reading the record is letting a valuation judgement override a fundamental case it rates B on every fundamental Element; a 25.9x multiple on a business growing EPS at 15 percent with 90 percent cash conversion is fair, not expensive; the Swedish acquirers have held 25 to 30x through cycles; Bufab's discount is closing because its margin and beat record now match theirs; and parking a business whose fundamentals are all B because its multiple is high is the error the framework's own momentum readings (technical B, earnings B) warn against.

What the record concedes: the record is real; the market is fragmented enough; the outer-year consensus does look low for a serial acquirer; every fundamental Element is B; the momentum readings say the market agrees with the earnings thesis; if the compounder rating holds the three-year return is about 7.7 to 8.9 percent a year, and if the deal pace doubles as well it is about 18 to 22 percent a year; if the deal pace doubled the record would move its earnings path from about 10 to about 13 percent a year and its odds on the compounder rating holding from about 30 to about 50 percent, and 'Compounder' would become the primary fit at B.
triggers: - Price: below about SEK 110 with the earnings path intact re-opens the case (about SEK 95 on the three-year value discounted at 20 percent; about SEK 110 on the eighteen-month value; about SEK 109 with the multiple held at 25.9x). The 52-week low was SEK 85.8.

- Q3 2026 report, 2026-10-23: gross margin at or above 32.5 percent (alarm below; invalidate below 30 percent, the risks research's catastrophic-loss threshold); organic growth above 4 percent excluding contract phasing (alarm below 2 percent in any quarter; invalidate two consecutive negative quarters in Europe); whether the Americas' tariff-driven margin fades (alarm below 16 percent); a beat or a miss against consensus with the multiple at the 98th percentile (alarm a 2 percent consensus cut; invalidate cuts across all three brokers).
- Breadth test for the hand-over: two quarters of organic growth above 4 percent with Europe West below 8 percent would show breadth; a group organic figure below 2 percent would show the opposite.

- Acquisition pace: two deals in H2 2026 adding SEK 500 million or more of annual sales would make 'Compounder' the primary fit, move the earnings path from about 10 to about 13 percent a year and the cleared odds from about 30 to about 50 percent; alarm twelve months without a deal; invalidate leverage above 3.0x without the EBITDA to match.

- The multiple and the cohort: a cohort re-rating lifting Addtech, Lagercrantz and Lifco toward 30x would make 25.9x a discount again; a cohort de-rating of 10 percent is the alarm; a short report on any Swedish serial acquirer, a Bossard profit warning or a European PMI relapse is sized at 15 to 20 percent by the Lifco precedent.

- The value-based pricing question: whether the gross margin holds when freight, tariff and deflation effects wash out through 2027; the price assumes consensus EBITDA margin on the brokers' basis rising from 15.9 percent (FY2025) to 18.2 percent (FY2028).
